scenario.win_condition: 3 orders dispatched in full before their deadlines, with material balance closed every tick
scenario.feasibility_check: Winning sequence hand-derived from stage order before shipping (mirror run is the arbiter): stage order per tick = order-deadline check, competing-task enqueue, carrier move, mill roll, dispatch task enqueue (at tick 1 for each open order), dispatch crane. Carrier moves start ticks 1,5,...,45 (12 moves = 120 t billet); rolls complete at 7,13,...,73 (12 x 9.8 = 117.6 t product). Dispatch tasks are enqueued at tick 1 (product yard is empty at start — first move cannot start before first product). Crane runs FIFO by priority: dispatch move completions at 4,7,10,13,16,19,22,25,28,31,34,37,40,43,46,49,52,55,58,61,64,67,70,73,76,79,82,85,88,91,94,97,100,103,106,109,112,115,118,121 (the last lands past tick 120 — 39 completions inside the run). The competing reorganize task (priority 1, created tick 40) overtakes the FIFO dispatch queue and runs ticks 40-43, delaying the tick-40 dispatch start to tick 44. O1 (30 t): completions at 4,7,10 = 30 t -> completed at tick 10 < deadline 60. O2 (30 t): completions at 13,16,19,22 = 39.2 t (whole-batch dispatch, no partial-batch splitting in v1) -> completed at tick 22 < 90. O3 (30 t): completions at 25,28,31,34 = 39.2 t -> completed at tick 34 < 120. Total dispatched inside the run = 39 moves x 9.8 t = 382.2 t. Product-yard capacity (60 t) is never binding here: max product-yard stock is 49 t at tick 72 (117.6 produced - 68.6 dispatched), so no refusal fires in the baseline — the capacity rule is proven by negative test N3, not by the baseline. Reachability check (standing rule): the contention block can only fire because the dispatch drain (3 ticks/move) is slower than the mill feed (4 ticks/move) and the yard has stock at tick 40 — verified by mirror run.
scenario.dispatch_rule_note: v1 dispatch rule is dispatch = min(stock, batch_t_per_move) — whole-batch moves, no partial-batch splitting. An order completes when cumulative dispatched_t >= required_t. A test that asserts 'backlog clears below required_t' contradicts this contract; expected values are derived from the contract arithmetic, not the narrative.

capacity_refusal_reachability.requires: product_yard capacity < stock accumulation at some tick
capacity_refusal_reachability.control_note: under lazy dispatch the drain matches production cadence exactly (3-tick move completes before the next 7-tick roll lands), so product_yard peak is a single 9.8t batch and capacity 60 t is unreachable — baseline asserts refusals == 0. The capacity-40 control as previously scripted does NOT fire (its arithmetic assumed the old pre-enqueue backlog narrative). Reachability proven separately: capacity 5 t -> 10 refusals at roll-completion ticks [11,18,...,74] with balance closed. Control re-tuning deferred to the later pass.

double_count_control.control_note: the seam (yard term counted twice) can only show a residual when product is resident in the yard at the measurement tick; under lazy dispatch the yard drains to 0 by tick 120, so the control run must give the crane a slower move (e.g. dispatch_crane.move_ticks=10 -> yard 8.4 t resident) for the broken rule to diverge (-8.4 residual). Verified with that variant; baseline-form control is weak. Documented.
